title: Blocking Synchronous I/O on the Main Thread Causes UI Stutter

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear, actionable description of a performance defect caused by synchronous I/O blocking the main Node.js event loop in shell.ts. It includes affected components, root cause, reproduction steps, and a clear fix.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix is a highly localized change in a single source file (packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts), replacing fs.mkdtempSync with await fsPromises.mkdtemp inside the asynchronous ShellToolInvocation.execute method. The root cause and solution are clear and straightforward.

summary.problem: Synchronous filesystem operation (fs.mkdtempSync) in shell tool execution blocks the main Node.js event loop, causing UI stuttering and input lag in the CLI interface.
summary.root_cause: ShellToolInvocation.execute calls fs.mkdtempSync synchronously on the main event loop immediately prior to spawning shell processes. Because React Ink UI rendering shares the main event loop, synchronous I/O blocks frame rendering and event handling.
summary.context: Since ShellToolInvocation.execute is already an asynchronous function, replacing fs.mkdtempSync with await fsPromises.mkdtemp non-blockingly resolves temporary directory creation without changing function signatures.

steps: In packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts, replace the synchronous call fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'gemini-shell-')) with await fsPromises.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'gemini-shell-')).
Ensure all temporary directory creation and error handling operate asynchronously in ShellToolInvocation.execute.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Shell execution creates temporary directories asynchronously via fsPromises.mkdtemp without blocking the event loop or causing UI stutter.
verification_steps: Run vitest packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts to verify that all shell tool unit tests pass.
